verses.1: When the night had dawned, the broad-chested, highly renowned, lotus-eyed Rama then spoke to his chief priest.
verses.2: He instructed that the shining sacred fire should go in front with the Brahmins, and the splendid Vajapeya umbrella should also be carried on the great path.
verses.3: Then, the lustrous Vasishtha completely performed all the rituals for the great departure according to scriptural injunctions.
verses.4: Then, wearing fine garments, meditating upon the supreme Brahman, and holding Kusa grass in his hands, he went forth.
verses.5: Not speaking anything, motionless, and devoid of joy on the path, he departed from that house, shining like the sun.
verses.6: On Rama's right side was Sri, the goddess of prosperity, holding a lotus; on his left was the great goddess Hri (Modesty); and in front of him was Determination.
verses.7: Various kinds of arrows, an excellent long bow, and all other weapons followed him, having assumed human forms.
verses.8: The Vedas in the form of Brahmins, the all-protecting Gayatri mantra, Omkara, and Vasatkara, all followed Rama with devotion.
verses.9: All the great-souled sages and Brahmins followed the great-souled Rama to the open gate of heaven.
verses.10: The women of the inner apartments, accompanied by their old and young maidservants, eunuchs, and chief servants, followed him as he went.
verses.11: Bharata, accompanied by Shatrughna and the women of his inner apartment, went, following Rama's path and bringing his sacred fire with him.
verses.12: All those great-souled individuals, having assembled with their sacred fires, sons, and wives, followed the great-minded Rama.
verses.13: All the ministers and groups of servants, along with their sons, animals, relatives, and followers, joyfully followed Rama.
verses.14: Then, all the subjects, filled with joyful and well-nourished people, who were charmed by Rama's virtues, followed him as he departed.
verses.15: Then, all of Rama's followers, including men, women, birds, animals, and those with vehicles, were joyful and purified of all sins.
verses.16: All the monkeys, bathed, greatly delighted, joyful, and well-nourished, loudly cheered with shouts of joy, all devoted to Rama.
verses.17: There was no one miserable, ashamed, or sorrowful; everything was joyful, prosperous, and extremely wonderful.
verses.18: Then, any rural person who arrived, desirous of seeing Rama departing, immediately followed him to heaven with joy upon seeing him.
verses.19: Bears, monkeys, rakshasas, and the city-dwellers, all well-composed, followed him from behind with supreme devotion.
verses.20: Even the invisible beings residing in the city followed Rama, who was ready to depart for heaven.
verses.21: All beings, both immobile and mobile, that beheld Rama, indeed followed him at his departure.
verses.22: Not even the slightest breathing creature was seen in Ayodhya, as all beings, even those of lower species, were devoted followers of Rama. इत्यार्षे श्रीमद्रामायणे वाल्मीकीये आदिकाव्ये श्रीमदुत्तरकाण्डे नवाधिकशततमः सर्गः ।। 109 ।। Thus ends the hundred and ninth sarga of Uttara Kanda of the holy Ramayana the first epic composed by sage Valmiki.
